title: Daft Punk - TH3 GR1D (Jaya Prime RMX)

content.text:
## Daft Punk - TH1 GR1D (Jaya Prime's Icon-of-Monkey Mix) \[[FREE DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/track/th3-gr1d-jaya-primes-icon-of-monkey-remix)\]

Going up against more than 1,000 other remixes in the coveted Daft Punk remix competition, my remix took runner-up at _Number Eleven Worldwide!_

We were not given permission to use samples from "TRON", otherwise I would have been adding in parts from Flynn's opening lines, befitting of any remix of "The Grid". Daft Punk's score for "TRON: Legacy" marked me, creating an impact point or landmark that -- from this point thereafter -- would alter the trajectory of my life... or at least my production skills. Blending electronic and symphonic elements, I've found their score on repeat more often than not. I study it to this day.

My remix would in fact have been ranked higher. BUT! They turned off voting on my mix because of how many people were coming to vote from graphic design websites, such as deviantART, and were voting firstly for my fractal design that I used in the album art... and only secondly for the music. In the end, they turned on voting again and allowed it to continue. However, that 48-hour ban took its toll.

_I'll wear my eleventh place with pride!_

All my music has different levels and media types of immersion. This was no different. It's funny how times change. At that time, I was more present on deviantART than on Instagram, but even on IG the art was getting attention. Then Lilyas, a writer and curator on deviantART, awarded the album art a "Daily Deviation" award and it took off from there.

_The rest is history._

\[[Download from Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/track/th3-gr1d-jaya-primes-icon-of-monkey-remix)\]

texts: "Not only a unique piece of art from the Tron universe, but a free song as well. The song and cover art pay brilliant and vivid homage to Daft Punk and the resurrection of the Tron mythos in the mainstream."

content.text:
Awarded for both the art and the music, to this day I still hold it dear as a prized accomplishment.

## "The Grid" Goes Public

I was honored to be included amongst those remixers. I do not take that for granted. When the competition ended, I turned around and paid that gift forward.

### The Song

I made the full remix available for free download, anything from an MP3 all the way up to WAV/FLAC. This follows the original license granted to me. You can download it for free [here on BandCamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/track/th3-gr1d-jaya-primes-icon-of-monkey-remix).

### The Design

I rendered the fractal design multiple ways, then released them for free download as a tile package that you, yourself can use. To this day, it's available for free download [here on deviantART](https://www.deviantart.com/jayaprime/art/TR0N-Disc-Grid-HD-Fractal-Tile-Stock-455263607).

texts: "Won't that be grand? Computers and the programs will start thinking and the people will stop."

content.text:
## With the Deepest Gratitude!

Mad thanks to LapsedPacifist, who unknowingly inspired the title; thanks to ignotus for the chanting; and to Stomp and ermine for the fireworks. Also, mad frakking thanks to all of these for the feedback: Caderageous, Gaea Qandromeda, DJ Ayanami, LapsedPacifist (again), R-E-L, Zaz Productions, JayKnight, CeeFer, Keeper of the Watch, Jordan Keller, Sean McCoy, Katie Gallanti, Christa Corsaro Tyson, Marf, Darth Murphy, Tristan Skybreak, Lita Harannie, Cyberius Rex, Temalika, plasmas, Devin Smith, Wadey, and Ovidiu Murzea. With love and gratitude to The Daughter of the Wind, herself, who also helped spread the word. Also, gotta shout out thanks to Daft Punk, Disney, and Indaba Music for putting the remix competition together.

As I write this, it is 2026, July 8. More than ever, "the grid" has become our reality. The programs are overwriting the flesh. I do not state this with judgment. These are merely the facts at this point in time.

_The lines between "program" and "user" and "grid" will only continue to blur._

texts: For those who've enjoyed my Daft Punk remix, I'd also suggest "[The Last Memory of Fire](last-memory-of-fire)" (from the "Alien" and "Predator" franchises), as well as my original production "[Time Interrupt](time-interrupt)". Both were heavily inspired along these same lines. Then may of my other award-winning fractal designs show up here under [pop art fractals](other-pop-art). For those who get into science fiction like "TRON", then my book "[Memoriam Redacta](memoriam-redacta)" might just be right up your glowing, neon-lit alley.
